tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description describes the triggering contexts in rich detail (model errors, 5xx, throttling, latency degradation, empty responses, post-deploy failures, bare status questions), focuses on the user's underlying goal (ruling whether fault is provider/infra/app before fix), and explicitly lists negative/positive trigger phrasings ('are we being throttled', 'is this AWS or us') as well as exclusions ('Do not load it for...'). While it starts descriptively ('Triage a live failure...') rather than literally 'Use this skill when', it functions imperatively as an instruction describing when/how to invoke, is pushy with explicit trigger enumeration, and remains within a reasonably concise paragraph given the complexity of the domain.
tests.evidence: "Triage a live failure where a model call is in the failing path - ... Use it when model invocations error or return 5xx, are throttled (429s), time out... Naming Bedrock, SageMaker or a model API is enough to load it. Do not load it for a symptom that names no model call yet..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (what Bedrock is, how HTTP errors work) and instead jumps directly into domain-specific procedures: the classifier, the ladder, binding resolution, and guardrails. Nearly every sentence carries non-obvious, skill-specific instruction.
tests.evidence: "You triage the LLM layer of a live failure on AWS. You run a classifier over the model path and return two things an investigation needs: where the fault sits, and whether it is transient."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (error codes, metric thresholds, API quirks, severity tables) is consistently pushed to references/ files and only summarized or named in the body. The classifier rules (R1-R5) are compact decision logic core to the skill, not a reference dump.
tests.evidence: "The detail of every step, with its branches and forbidden exits, is in [classifier-walkthrough.md](references/classifier-walkthrough.md); API arguments and rationale are in [transient-vs-config-classifier.md](references/transient-vs-config-classifier.md)."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked with a markdown link in the body, e.g. hosting-bindings.md, request-path.md, router.md, classifier-walkthrough.md, error-codes.md, transient-vs-config-classifier.md, incident-signatures.md, checks-telemetry.md, metrics-and-logs.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, common-wrong-answers.md, severity-definitions.md, related-skills.md all appear as markdown links.
tests.evidence: "[hosting-bindings.md](references/hosting-bindings.md) — **Step 0**: the signal triple, the binding table, which locus members each binding can reach"

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific trigger condition for when to load it, not just a generic 'see for details' phrasing.
tests.evidence: "Read it before the first API call." ... "Walking Steps 1-6 against AWS/Bedrock for a model served from a container produces a ledger ... bind first: [hosting-bindings.md](references/hosting-bindings.md)."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative 'references/filename.md' format with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: The skill is highly prescriptive about the fragile classifier ladder (exact rule ordering, closed token sets) while giving more interpretive freedom in areas like related-skills handling and conclusion framing, matching rigidity to fragility.
tests.evidence: "The ladder is total; the first rule that holds wins." paired with "Depth on another stage is optional. Name the stage and its owner track ... When the evidence points there, follow Related skills (optional)"

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple hosting bindings or approaches exist, the skill designates a clear default (bedrock binding) and treats alternatives as substitutions, not an undifferentiated menu.
tests.evidence: "Bind, then route. ... every metric name below is the bedrock binding's, and the row is still correct for another binding only once its triple is substituted."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable triage procedure (bind → classify → rule → conclude) applicable to any incident matching the load condition, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: "Run it on every availability or invocation-failure incident before attributing the cause to customer configuration."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive, explicit gotchas-style section covering non-obvious API/metric misreadings specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: "CloudWatch 'no datapoints' ≠ zero (§10). No datapoints usually means no traffic / metric not emitted — not a measured zero."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: Structured output templates are provided via assets (triage-report-template.md) and referenced for when a full report is needed, satisfying the structured-output requirement.
tests.evidence: "[triage-report-template.md](assets/triage-report-template.md) is the long form of the same shape, for when a full written report is wanted."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body does not contain a large inline output template; it only describes the three-block contract shape briefly and defers the full template to assets/.
tests.evidence: "Exit: three blocks, every time. The TRIAGE: line first, then the prose, then the Findings block with one line per signal."

tests.name: Asset files must be linked

tests.evidence: "[delegation-payload.json](assets/delegation-payload.json) is that prompt, finished: read it, fill the four <…> placeholders"

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Both asset links specify clear conditions for when to load them (delegation scenario, or when a full written report is wanted).
tests.evidence: "[triage-report-template.md](assets/triage-report-template.md) is the long form of the same shape, for when a full written report is wanted."

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The core procedural workflow (the classifier) is presented as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, and the detailed walkthrough file is explicitly tied to those same step numbers.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 0: **Bind.** Resolve the hosting binding...\n- [ ] Step 1: Check provider health..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an extensive explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to re-check its own draft output against a checklist before presenting it.
tests.evidence: "Before you present a triage result, re-check your own classifier output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
